normalFinding.default: Abdomen flat and symmetric without scars, distension, discoloration or visible pulsations.

steps: Expose the abdomen from the lower chest to the pelvis with the patient lying flat.
Look at contour and symmetry, including from the side at abdominal level.
Note any scars, skin changes or visible masses.

normalFinding.default: Normoactive bowel sounds in all four quadrants.

steps: Place the stethoscope diaphragm lightly on the abdomen.
Listen for a short while in every quadrant.
Note the presence and character of bowel sounds.

normalFinding.default: No aortic, renal or iliac bruits.

steps: Listen with the stethoscope over the aorta just above the umbilicus.
Listen over each renal artery, slightly above and to either side of the umbilicus.
Listen over each iliac artery below the umbilicus.

normalFinding.default: Abdomen soft and non-tender without guarding or rigidity.

steps: Watch the patient's face throughout and leave any painful area until last.
With the flat of your fingers, press gently in each quadrant using a rocking motion.

normalFinding.default: No masses or deep tenderness in any quadrant.

steps: After light palpation, press more firmly in each quadrant.
Feel for masses or deep tenderness, keeping an eye on the patient's face.

normalFinding.default: Murphy's sign negative; inspiration not interrupted by pain.

steps: Place your fingers below the right costal margin at the midclavicular line.
Ask the patient to breathe in slowly while you press in and up under the ribs.
Watch for the breath being stopped short because of pain.
Find the point about one third of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.
Press firmly there and ask about pain.
Have the patient sit up and lay one palm over the angle between the lowest rib and the spine.
Strike the back of that hand with the ulnar side of your other fist.
Ask about pain and repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Liver edge not palpable or felt as a smooth, soft, non-tender edge at the right costal margin.

steps: Start low in the right lower quadrant at the midclavicular line.
Ask the patient to breathe in and feel for the edge striking your fingertips.
Move your hand up a little at a time until the edge or costal margin is reached.
Stand on the patient's right and reach across to support the left lower ribs from behind.
With your right hand below the left costal margin, ask for a deep breath.
Feel for a spleen tip moving down onto your fingers.

normalFinding.default: Aortic pulsation palpable in the epigastrium, not expansile, of normal width.

steps: Stand on the patient's right and press firmly just left of midline in the upper abdomen.
Once you feel the pulse, place a hand on either side of it.
Judge the width and whether the pulsation pushes your hands apart.
